newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says 7-8 pct GNP target attainable.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says 7-8 pct GNP target attainable.

text.p: The Philippines can still achieve its growth national product (GNP) growth target this year of seven to eight percent despite the recent sharp depreciation of the peso, a senior government official said on Monday.
"The seven to eight percent GNP is still attainable. The depreciation would lead us to the six to 6.5 percent original inflation target," Planning Secretary Cielito Habito told businessmen.
Habito had earlier said the government would improve its inflation target this year to 5.2 percent to 5.7 percent.
Inflation in the first six months averaged 4.6 percent.

The government effectively devalued the peso just over a week ago after a wave of speculative attacks in the currency. It had previously insisted that a stable peso was essential to controlling inflation.
Habito also said the depreciation would help the manufacturing sector.
Since last year, the manufacturing segment had been dragged down mainly by closures and strikes at garment factories as Philippine clothing exports becmae overpriced.
"We are already out of the transitory period. Strikes and closures of companies are over and those manufacturing are back in operation and so the numbers are looking good once more," he said.
